clue.text: I am a brute — the odds are steep

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the phrase I am a brute are taken, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A brutish speaker gloomily admits the odds against him are steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the odds are' looks like betting talk but tells you to keep letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 'I am a brute'.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak or saturate it, the same sense as to imbue it.

clue.text: See 24
Political group's blunder backfiring may be cause of unexpected explosion

definitions.text: may be cause of unexpected explosion

indicators.note: something backfiring goes the wrong way, so the word for the group is read backwards

parts.note: a political group is a party
a boob is a silly mistake

explanation.surface: A party's gaffe blows up in its face, like a bomb going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' turns the whole phrase, party's boob, back to front; BOOB reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden device rigged to go off when touched is the classic cause of an unexpected blast.

clue.text: Manage to put back the hour on time

indicators.note: putting a word back means writing it in reverse order

parts.note: to manage is to cope
h is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Instructions for changing the clocks at the end of summer time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' sounds like turning the clocks back an hour, but it reverses COPE to EPOC.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a period of time, an era.

clue.text: For those who have to eat their hats?

definitions.text: For those who have to eat their hats?

parts.words: For those who have to eat their hats?
parts.note: people who boast they will eat their hat if proved wrong may need hats that are edible, made of pastry with a meat filling

explanation.surface: Headgear for people who lose a rash bet and must eat their hats.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie hats are flat-crowned hats; pork pies are also British meat pastries, and in Cockney rhyming slang 'pork pies' means lies, which the other clues use.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat shaped like a pie with a flat crown is named after the pastry, so an eaten hat might as well be one.

clue.text: Religious post for naval leader?

definitions.meaning: the office held by a prior, head of a priory
a vessel in front of the others could whimsically be called the prior one

explanation.surface: A churchy job is offered to an admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of a prior in a religious house is his office; read as two words it is a ship ahead of others.

clue.text: Wander to the end of the road, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the place name is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: all roads lead to Rome, so the Italian capital is where every road ends

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to stroll all the way to the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'all roads lead to Rome' makes Rome the end of the road; it sounds like ROAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel about aimlessly, to wander.

clue.text: Dew shaken into first part of 4 across, say, may be cause of explosion

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: the first word of pork pies

indicators.note: shaken means the letters of dew are jumbled

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Damp gets into a store of gunpowder, which may still blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' jumbles 'Dew', and 'into' puts the result inside the first word of 4 across, pork pies; 'say' is the usual signal for eg, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrel of gunpowder, or by extension a tense situation, is something that can blow up.

clue.text: Praise from former partner to student

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
L is the learner plate sign, used for a student

explanation.surface: Kind words about the ex passed on to a student.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, used here as the verb.

clue.text: Giving value for money, T.H.White's work on model girl is producing 4 across

parts.note: economical means thrifty, good value

indicators.note: work signals the letters of the author's initials and surname are worked over into a new order

parts.note: the name of the author of The Once and Future King, initials included
the Model T was Ford's famous car
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheap edition of T.H. White's novel about a model named Ruth turns out to be full of fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges THWHITE into WITHTHE. 4 across, pork pies, is rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a famous euphemism for lying, coined by a civil servant in the Spycatcher trial.

clue.text: Can't decide if foolish girl's drunk?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs his esses into sh sounds, so the name is spoken that way

parts.note: a foolish girl might be called Silly Sally

explanation.surface: Unable to make up one's mind whether a silly girl has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'Silly Sally' with a drunken slur and every S becomes SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To shilly-shally is to waver and be indecisive.

clue.text: New Year, when the scene is immaterial

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: New Year's Eve, when it does not matter where you celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of 'New Year' but is the anagram signal for YEAR WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: If any place at all will do, the location does not matter.

clue.text: Condition of the left in Ted's grip

indicators.note: in and grip together mean one piece is held inside another
grip, with in, says the surname holds the letter

parts.note: Ted Heath was British Conservative prime minister 1970-74
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The state of the Labour left under Heath's grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward 'Ted' Heath was a British Conservative prime minister; L goes inside HEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: One's health is one's physical condition.

clue.text: Far from pristine outbuilding on lake island

indicators.note: on means placed after the other pieces in this across entry

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
a shed is an outbuilding

explanation.surface: A ramshackle hut on an island in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tarnished is dulled or sullied, the opposite of pristine.

clue.text: Not enough blood here: I get half with tea in it first

annotationWithheld.why: Not enough blood here: I get half with tea in it first (9): I + SEMI round CHA gives ISCHAEMI, but no clue word fairly supplies the final A
annotationWithheld.clue: Not enough blood here: I get half with tea in it first

clue.text: Poor old hat web gets the coup de grace

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of old hat web are in bad shape, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tired old spider's web finally gets finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup de grace is a finishing stroke, a killing blow.

clue.text: A lark damaged the village

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of a lark are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A songbird wrecks something in a village.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional enclosed village in southern Africa.

clue.text: Broadcaster in a year with some doubt

parts.note: anno is Latin for in the year, as in anno Domini

indicators.note: some means only part of the word for doubt is used, its ending dropped

parts.note: doubt is uncertainty

explanation.surface: A broadcaster who spends a year full of doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNO is Latin, as in AD (anno Domini); 'some' keeps just UNCER of UNCERTAINTY.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer is someone who presents on radio or television, a broadcaster.

clue.text: Theme to select: abolition of the monarchy?

indicators.note: abolishing the monarchy removes the king, so K is dropped

parts.note: to select is to pick

explanation.surface: A suggested subject for debate: should the monarchy be abolished?
explanation.walkthrough: K is the chess abbreviation for king, so 'abolition of the monarchy' takes K out of PICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject or theme of discussion.

clue.text: Scheme to get the lowdown on some cyclist's reported clanger

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
gen is British slang for information, the lowdown

indicators.note: some means only part of the word cyclist's is used

explanation.surface: A plot to find out about a cyclist's alleged blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clanger' looks like a blunder, but 'reported clanger' is the sound of 'clangour', a loud resonant ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangency is a loud, resonant, mournful quality of sound, which is what clangour means.

clue.text: Is medium in time to give alarm?

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the word for time

parts.note: a day is a period of time
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant at a séance tries to frighten the sitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a psychic, but it is M, the size.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay is to fill with alarm or consternation.

clue.text: Weapon used by the Mint?

definitions.meaning: a long-shafted pointed throwing or thrusting weapon
the word comes before mint in the name of a garden herb

explanation.surface: The Royal Mint keeps a weapon handy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mint suggests the place where coins are made, but here it is spearmint.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a weapon, and the first half of spearmint.

clue.text: See 8
One over the eight? A near thing

definitions.meaning: British slang for having had a drink too many, so drunk
a close call, as in a ... finish

explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk and also describes a contest that is very close.

clue.text: The responsibility is America's

definitions.meaning: something that is America's to pay for is on the US

explanation.surface: Washington is told the burden falls on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Onus is Latin for burden and means a duty or responsibility.

clue.text: (and 1 down) Singular 4 across in charge of little go (crude examination)

indicators.note: singular means odd or strange, so the letters are made into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An old Cambridge preliminary exam, the Little Go, was a crude test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like it makes 4 across one lie, but it is the anagram signal for IC + LITTLE GO CRUDE EXAMINATION. The Little Go was Cambridge's entrance exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill's phrase is a famously pompous euphemism for a lie, which is what 4 across means in rhyming slang.

clue.text: Bachelor studies, having a wife for preparing food

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A student becomes a married man who learns to cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated kitchen knife for slicing loaves is a tool used in preparing food.

clue.text: Wait with viscosity

explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to wait or linger; as an adjective it means covered in or resembling tar.
